text:
jess: Quick sync — we keep burning time spinning up full SEV war rooms for partner-facing incidents. Can we define lightweight response lanes for Marketplace + HW/SI issues? Not every problem needs a full bridge.

omar: +1. What do you mean by "lanes" here? a set of Slack channels / notification rules? :thinking_face:

jess: Exactly. Two tiers: Lane A = customer-impacting partner incidents (prod outage, data exposure). Lane B = integration/partner-dev issues (broken onboarding, listing errors). Lane A gets paging + short-lived bridge. Lane B goes to a shared channel and async triage.

ravi: Sounds good. For Lane A we should auto-create an ephemeral channel that includes: partner PM, partner SE, our oncall, and the marketplace ops rep. Minimal invite list.

frank: From Support side — we need clear ownership windows. If a partner rep is unavailable, the SRE oncall or partner success covers first 30 mins, then escalate to oncall rotation.

kate: Can we automate the ephemeral bridge creation? partner-bot can create channels with a template and pre-populated runbook link.

partner-bot: NOTE: new-bridge workflow available. Usage:
```
/partner-bridge create --name "ephemeral-<partner>-<yyyymmdd>" \
  --tier A --owner @ravi --ttl 8h --runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/partner-sev
```

omar: Love that. Also add a step to pin the current incident ticket + partner contact details in the channel header.

jess: Proposal for notification routing (short):
- Lane A: Pager -> #partnerships-lane-a (ephemeral bridge auto-created), email to partner oncall, post to status page.
- Lane B: #partnerships-lane-b (persistent), assign triage owner within 2h, sync next business day if unresolved.

ravi: For hardware partners we need an extra step: include HW integrations SME and file a labeled bug in our partner integrator board (label: partner-hw). That way PLs can track fixes across vendors.

frank: Agreed. Also checklist for Lane A bridge starter:
1) Create ephemeral bridge (partner-bot)
2) Tag severity and impacted customers
3) Add runbook link + paging log
4) Capture first 15m summary and post to #partnerships (ops-summary thread)
5) Assign follow-up owner for postmortem

kate: Small UX note — make sure our partner-facing runbook language is non-technical so partner PMs can follow along before we add SEs to the room.

omar: Ops automation idea: if the incoming alert has tag marketplace or hw, partner-bot should suggest bridge creation in the alerting channel with one-click confirm. Saves 2–3 min.

jess: Ok action items:
- ravi: draft a one-page partner response lane doc (Lane A / Lane B + roles) by Fri.
- omar: prototype partner-bot confirm flow for alerts (ETA next week).
- frank: create a support-side escalation window doc and typical handoff script.
- kate: review runbook language for partners.

ravi: Will do. I'll put a short template for the post-incident partner message we can reuse.

frank: Example handoff script (short):
"Thanks — we've created an ephemeral bridge (link). Our SRE oncall, partner success, and your SE are in. We'll post a 15m status update and the incident owner for follow-up is @frank".

kate: One more ask — can we get a marketplace contact matrix (who owns listing, billing, integrations) per partner and store it in the runbook? That cuts churn when we reach out.

jess: Yes. I'll add a spreadsheet link to the runbook and add column requirements.

partner-bot: REMINDER: running dry-run simulation Friday 09:00 UTC. Reaction :bell: to opt in.

ravi: I'll join the simulation. Planning to include one HW partner and one marketplace listing failure scenario.

omar: I'll mock the alert flow. frank — can you play the support lead?

frank: Yep.

jess: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the doc + prototype. If anyone is blocked ping me or drop a reaction. :thumbsup:
